I bought it, but I was able to get it for $30. The asking price of $60 is outrageous, and will seriously hurt the game's longevity due to the smaller playerbase.
I remember playing Vegas 2 and thinking it was some kind of revolutionary combat mechanics (coming off of CoD) how would you rate Siege in this area?

I'm enjoying it right now, especially playing with buddies. There are only two main game modes, Terrorist Hunt (human vs AI) and multiplayer. I haven't gotten into the multiplayer yet.

You have to coordinate with your team in order to complete the mission objective, which feels a lot like Payday 2. Gameplay is tactical, and it's easy to die by just one enemy who managed to get the drop on you.

Each game is separated into attackers vs defenders, with the AI providing the opposite team in terrorist hunt. Attackers have to defuse a bomb, rescue a hostage, or eliminate the terrorists. Defenders have to prevent the attackers from completing their objective. Attackers have door breach charges, demolitions, and they focus on creating alternate routes and setting up coordinated strikes in order to attack the objective. Defenders can fortify, trap, and ambush to hinder the attackers.

You can play as one of 10 defender operators, and one of 10 attacker operators, each with their own special ability geared towards attack or defense.

I'd say where it's hurting the most is lack of levels and game modes, but since you spend most of your time in very close quarters the lack of levels isn't too bad. And you do a fair bit of reshaping the level in different ways each time anyway. The bigger issue is that if you get burned out on the gameplay, you'll get sick of the game easily. Imagine CoD: Black Ops 3, if it only had multiplayer. Some people could play it every day forever and not be put off at all, but other people would get sick of it and miss the other game modes like campaign and zombies.

I only played the first Vegas (and loved it), but I don't remember anything about it. I also haven't played any of the Rainbow Six games, so I'll just describe how Siege works:

  1. Attackers get mostly assault rifles while defenders get mostly SMGs. The difference in damage output is noticeable and gives attackers a substantial advantage. All headshots are one-shot kills, so as a defender you're usually better off going for a headshot.
  2. You only get one life per round. Don't remember how Vegas/Vegas 2 worked, but I think that was the case there as well.
  3. There is no cover system, but you can use the Q and E keys to lean.
  4. The ability to use drones (as an attacker) to scout the area is really neat, and essentially acts as an extra life if you scout out a roaming defender that would have killed you otherwise.
  5. The game has been plagued by lag problems, particularly peeker's advantage. This seems to have gotten better with the last patch.

All in all I'd say the gunplay feels very solid, far better than CS:GO and BF4, both of which I abhor. Also better than CoD, where every gun feels like a peashooter.

I'd also like to add that this is the first FPS I've played where it is frequently a good idea to switch to your pistol rather than reloading your primary.
